data.name: Epanalepsis
data.detailed_description:
Rachel goes out drinking every night. Anthony plays his videogames. The machinery beneath the world keeps right on ticking. Epanalepsis is a narrative-focused point and click adventure game that tells a story about those connections across sixty years and beyond that pays equal homage to New Wave science fiction, cyberpunk dystopian stories, and the art cinema of the early 1990s.

FEATURES

  • Play as three characters in three radically different time periods. Experience an authentically recreated 1990s, a consumerist 2010s, and a cyberpunk 2030s.
  • Hand-crafted visuals wrung from the cramping hands of a very committed developer.
  • Narrative-focused adventure gaming without the stress and trauma of puzzles or inventory management.

reviews.review:
Epanalepsis is an unconventional narrative adventure developed by Cameron Kunzelman and published by Mastertronic that focuses far more on storytelling and philosophical reflection than traditional gameplay. Rather than emphasizing difficult puzzles or fast-paced mechanics, the game presents an interactive experience built around three separate stories set in different time periods. Each protagonist initially appears disconnected from the others, but as the narrative unfolds, recurring themes, mysterious encounters, and symbolic events gradually reveal deeper relationships between their lives. The result is an experience that values interpretation and contemplation, inviting players to discover meaning beneath its quiet and often enigmatic surface.

The game's greatest strength is its willingness to explore complex ideas through its writing. Each chapter introduces a unique protagonist facing personal struggles that reflect the social and technological climate of their respective era. The first story explores dissatisfaction and uncertainty in the early 1990s, while the second shifts toward a more modern setting where technology and everyday routines influence personal identity. The final chapter transports players into a futuristic world, where a robotic character raises thought-provoking questions about consciousness, purpose, and humanity itself. Although the settings and characters differ considerably, they are connected by recurring symbols and conversations that examine whether life follows a predetermined pattern or if individuals truly possess free will. The game rarely provides direct answers, instead encouraging players to interpret events through their own perspective.

The minimalist presentation complements the narrative exceptionally well. Its pixel art is simple yet expressive, creating environments that feel authentic despite their limited visual complexity. Every location contains small environmental details that reveal aspects of the characters' personalities and the passage of time, rewarding players who carefully examine their surroundings. The transitions between decades are handled effectively, showing subtle changes in technology, architecture, and culture while maintaining a consistent artistic style. Rather than relying on visual spectacle, Epanalepsis uses restraint to establish atmosphere, allowing players to become immersed in each setting through observation instead of elaborate graphics.

Sound design also plays an important role in shaping the overall mood. The soundtrack remains understated throughout the adventure, providing gentle musical accompaniment that enhances emotional moments without overwhelming the dialogue. Ambient sounds help reinforce feelings of isolation, uncertainty, and quiet reflection, creating an experience that feels intimate and contemplative. Combined with the measured pacing of conversations, the audio encourages players to slow down and absorb both the spoken words and the subtle emotional undertones behind them.

Gameplay is intentionally straightforward, focusing almost entirely on exploration, interaction, and dialogue. Players move through side-scrolling environments, inspect objects, speak with various characters, and occasionally make decisions that influence the flow of conversations. There are very few traditional adventure game mechanics, with almost no emphasis on inventory puzzles or complicated problem-solving. This simplicity allows the narrative to remain at the forefront, making the experience accessible to players who primarily enjoy story-driven games. However, those looking for substantial gameplay systems or greater player freedom may find the interaction too limited, as the game consistently prioritizes narrative progression over mechanical depth.

One of the most memorable aspects of Epanalepsis is its confidence in embracing ambiguity. Rather than neatly explaining every mystery, it leaves many events open to interpretation, encouraging players to revisit previous scenes and reconsider the significance of recurring characters, conversations, and symbols. The title itself reflects the game's fascination with repetition, cycles, and recurring patterns, themes that become increasingly apparent as the different storylines begin to echo one another. This literary approach gives the game a distinctive identity, though it may frustrate players who prefer clear answers and definitive conclusions.

The relatively short length also affects the overall experience. While each protagonist is interesting and their stories introduce compelling ideas, some character arcs conclude before reaching their full emotional potential. Several relationships and philosophical concepts could have benefited from additional development, allowing players to form stronger connections with the cast before the story reaches its conclusion. Likewise, the links between the three narratives rely more on thematic resonance than explicit storytelling, making the ending especially dependent on the player's willingness to interpret its symbolism.

Despite these limitations, Epanalepsis stands out as an ambitious independent adventure that confidently pursues its own creative vision. It is not designed for players seeking action, difficult challenges, or conventional storytelling. Instead, it rewards patience, curiosity, and thoughtful reflection, offering an experience that lingers long after its relatively brief runtime has ended. Its willingness to prioritize philosophical ideas over mainstream accessibility gives it a unique place among narrative-focused indie games.

Rating: 6/10
